title: Create and await a vSAN Data Protection protection-group snapshot
prompt:
Implement `New-VsanProtectionGroupSnapshot` in `src/VsanDataProtection/VsanDataProtection.psm1` without changing its supplied signature. The genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` PowerCLI module version `13.4.0.24798382` is installed as an environment prerequisite and is required by the supplied module manifest. Use its generated `Initialize-VcfAssociatedTask` model initializer for the task reference returned by vSAN Data Protection; do not install, copy, vendor, redefine, or replace the VMware SDK module.

Follow the focused VCF 9.0 contract in `docs/contract.json` for exactly the operationIds `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task` and `Snapservice.Tasks_get`. The contract was derived from `specifications/vsan-data-protection/vsan-data-protection-openapi.yaml` at tag `9.0.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, at the tag commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`; it is not based on a documentation page or the 9.1 revision. Treat `ServerUri` as the appliance origin. URI-escape each path identifier as one segment, send the session in `vmware-api-session-id`, and send `Accept: application/json` on every request. Requests with JSON bodies must send `Content-Type: application/json`; task GET requests must have no body or Content-Type.

Create the manual snapshot with a compact JSON body containing exactly the required `name`. The contract's optional `retention` field is unset by this function and must be omitted entirely rather than serialized as null, an empty object, an empty string, or a default value. Do not synthesize any other request members.

The create response is asynchronous and contains only a task identifier. Build the SDK task-reference model from that identifier, reject an empty identifier, and poll that same task with `Snapservice.Tasks_get` at least once; never treat the create response as completion. `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, and `BLOCKED` are nonterminal. Continue polling until `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED`, sleeping for `PollIntervalMilliseconds` only after a nonterminal task response and before the next lookup. Return the terminal task object on `SUCCEEDED`, throw on `FAILED`, and reject a status outside the contract. Do not add a polling-call ceiling.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier uses the genuine installed VMware SDK module and a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port. It reads the mock request log to check the exact HTTP methods, escaped targets, headers, compact JSON body, polling sequence, and omission of unset optional fields. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `docs/`, `mock/`, and `tests/`, plus the module manifest, is protected. Edit only `src/VsanDataProtection/VsanDataProtection.psm1`.
scenario: A manual protection-group snapshot is accepted asynchronously and must be polled from RUNNING to a terminal SUCCEEDED task state.
